English: Hill Camp
A makeshift encampment of tents and wooden shelters, nestled defensively on a hilltop. The first step in establishing a secure foothold in the wild hills.
Earthwork Bank
Dug trenches and piled earth banks reinforce the camps perimeter, offering modest resistance to raiders and wild beasts alike.
Hilltop Palisade
A stout wooden palisade encircling the earthworks, manned by local levies and simple watchtowers to spot approaching threats.
Stone Ringfort
Low stone walls replace the old palisade, forming a ringfort with improved defensive positions and protected entryways.
Guarded Hillfort
A robust stone fortification with towers at intervals and reinforced gates, guarded by trained watchmen.
Wooded Bastion
Solid timber and stone bastions are built atop the slopes, using the dense local woods as both resource and camouflage for defenders.
Hilltop Tower
A tall stone tower rises above the hill, serving as a formidable keep, command post, and beacon for all the surrounding lands.
Hillside Keep
An imposing stone keep with multiple layers of walls, storerooms, barracks, and a central tower dominating the hillside.
Hill Citadel
A mighty citadel crowns the hill, its bastions and curtain walls bristling with defenders and archery slits, commanding the valleys below.
Cairn Fortress
The ultimate expression of hill fortification: a massive fortress built amidst ancient cairns, its walls and towers dominating the region and offering unmatched defense and prestige.
